q: Find the simple interest on Rs. 5200 for 2 years at 6% per annum.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{P = Principal}}\,{\text{Amount}} \\ & {\text{T = }}\,{\text{Time}}\,{\text{period}} \\ & {\text{R = Rate}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{Interest}} \\ & I = \frac{{P \times T \times R}}{{100}} \\ & I = \frac{{5200 \times 2 \times 6}}{{100}} \\ & I = 624. \end{aligned}$$

q: Rs. 1200 is lent out at 5% per annum simple interest for 3 years. Find the amount after 3 years.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & A = P + I \\ & A = 1200 + {\frac{{PTR}}{{100}}} \\ & A = {1200 + {\frac{{1200 \times 5 \times 3}}{{100}}} } \\ & {\text{Amount}},\,A = Rs.\,1380 \end{aligned}$$

q: Interest obtained on a sum of Rs. 5000 for 3 years is Rs. 1500. Find the rate percent.

q: Rs. 2100 is lent at compound interest of 5% per annum for 2 years. Find the amount after two years.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{We}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{use}}\,{\text{formula}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{compound}}\,{\text{interest}} \\ & A = P \times {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^n} \\ & A = 2100 \times {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{5}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^2} \\ & A = 2100 \times {\left[ {\frac{{105}}{{100}}} \right]^2} \\ & A = \frac{{ {2100 \times 11025} }}{{10000}} \\ & {\text{Hence,}}\,{\text{Amount}}\,A = Rs.\,2315.25 \end{aligned}$$

q: Find the difference between the simple interest and the compound interest at 5% per annum for 2 years on principal of Rs. 2000.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{The}}\,{\text{difference}}\,{\text{between}}\,{\text{compound}}\,{\text{interest}}\,{\text{and}} \\ & {\text{simple}}\,{\text{interest}}\,{\text{over}}\,{\text{two}}\,{\text{years}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{given}}\,{\text{by}} \\ & \frac{{{{\Pr }^2}}}{{{{100}^2}}}\,or\,P{\left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)^2} \\ & {\text{Here,}}\,{\text{Principal}}\,\left( P \right) = Rs.\,2000 \\ & {\text{Rate}}\,\left( r \right) = 5\% \\ & {\text{Now}}\,{\text{difference}}, \\ & D = \frac{{ {2000 \times 5 \times 5} }}{{ {100 \times 100} }} \\ & D = Rs.\,5 \end{aligned}$$

q: Find the rate of interest if the amount after 2 years of simple interest on a capital of Rs. 1200 is Rs. 1440.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Amount}},\,A = Rs.\,1440 \\ & {\text{Principal}},\,P = Rs.\,1200 \\ & {\text{Interest}},\,I = Rs.\,\left( {1440 - 1200} \right) = 240 \\ & R = \frac{{ {240 \times 100} }}{{ {1200 \times 2} }} = 10\% \\ & \\ & {\text{Alternatively}}, \\ & {\text{We}}\,{\text{can}}\,{\text{go}}\,{\text{through}}\,{\text{a}}\,{\text{thought}}\,{\text{process}}\,i.e. \\ & 1200\, == 20\% \uparrow \left( {240\,{\text{in}}\,2\,{\text{years}}} \right) ⇒ 1400 \\ & {\text{That}}\,{\text{means}}\,10\% \,{\text{rise}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{each}}\,{\text{year}} \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the difference between the simple interest on a principal of Rs. 500 being calculated at 5% per annum for 3 years and 4% per annum for 4 years?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {I_1} = \frac{{P{T_1}{R_1}}}{{100}} \\ & {I_1} = \frac{{ {500 \times 3 \times 5} }}{{100}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\, = Rs.{\kern 1pt} 75 \\ & {I_2} = \frac{{P{T_2}{R_2}}}{{100}} \\ & {I_2} = \frac{{ {500 \times 4 \times 4} }}{{100}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = Rs.{\kern 1pt} 80 \\ & {\text{Difference}} = 80 - 75 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,5 \end{aligned}$$ Alternatively The interest is calculated simply and then it will have a rise of 15% in 1 st case and 16% in 2 nd case. Difference = 1% on 500 = Rs. 5 Otherway, 500 == 15% $$\uparrow$$ ⇒ 575 (1 st case) 500 == 16% $$\uparrow$$ ⇒ 580 (2 nd case) We can see clear difference of Rs. 5

q: What is the simple interest on a sum of Rs. 700 if the rate of interest for the first 3 years is 8% per annum and for the last 2 years is 7.5% per annum?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {1^{{\text{st}}}}{\kern 1pt} {\text{case}}: \\ & {I_1} = \frac{{700 \times 3 \times 8}}{{100}} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}168 \\ & {2^{{\text{nd}}}}{\kern 1pt} {\text{case}}: \\ & {I_2} = \frac{{700 \times 2 \times 7.5}}{{100}} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}105 \end{aligned}$$ Then total interest for five years $$= \left( {{I_1} + {I_2}} \right) = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}273$$ Alternatively, As interest is calculated as simple interest So, we can add up rates for all given 5 years and calculate it easily i.e. For the five years rate = (8 × 3 + 7.5 × 2) = 39% Now, 700 = 39% $$\uparrow$$ ⇒ 973 Interest = Rs. 273 The thought can go this way we internally calculated $$\begin{aligned} & {\kern 1pt} 10\% \,{\text{of}}\,700 = {\frac{{700}}{{10}}} = 70 \\ & {\text{Then}}, \\ & 39\% \,{\text{of}}\,700 \\ & = \left( {40\% - 1\% } \right)\,{\text{of}}\,700 \\ & = \left( {280 - 7} \right) \\ & = 273 \end{aligned}$$

q: Find the compound interest on Rs. 1000 at the rate of 20% per annum for 18 month when interest is compounded half yearly.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Given,}}\,{\text{Principal}},\,P = Rs.\,1000 \\ & {\text{Compoind}}\,{\text{rate}},\,R = 20\% \,{\text{per}}\,{\text{annum}} \\ & = \frac{{20}}{2} = 10\% \,{\text{half - yearly}} \\ & {\text{Time}} = 18\,{\text{month}} = 3\,{\text{half - years}} \\ & {\text{Amount}}, \\ & A = \left\{ {P \times {{\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{R}{{100}}} \right)} \right]}^n}} \right\} \\ & = \left\{ {1000 \times {{\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{{10}}{{100}}} \right)} \right]}^3}} \right\} \\ & = { {\frac{{1000 \times 11 \times 11 \times 11}}{{10 \times 10 \times 10}}} } \\ & A = Rs.\,1331 \\ & {\text{Hence,}}\,{\text{compound}}\,{\text{interest}} = Rs.\,331 \end{aligned}$$

q: Find the principal if the interest compounded at the rate of 10% per annum for two years is Rs. 420.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Given}}, \\ & {\text{Compound}}\,{\text{rate}},\,R = 10\% \,{\text{per}}\,{\text{annum}} \\ & {\text{Time}} = 2\,{\text{years}} \\ & CI - Rs.\,420 \\ & {\text{Let}}\,P\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{required}}\,{\text{principal}} \\ & A = \left( {P + CI} \right) \\ & {\text{Amount}},A = \left\{ {P \times {{\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{R}{{100}}} \right)} \right]}^n}} \right\} \\ & \left( {P + CI} \right) = \left\{ {P \times {{\left[ {1 + \frac{{10}}{{100}}} \right]}^2}} \right\} \\ & \left( {P + 420} \right) = P \times {\left[ {\frac{{11}}{{10}}} \right]^2} \\ & P - 1.21P = - 420 \\ & 0.21P = 420 \\ & {\text{Hence}},P = \frac{{420}}{{0.21}} = Rs.\,2000 \end{aligned}$$

q: In what time will Rs. 3300 becomes Rs. 3399 at 6% per annum interest compounded half-yearly?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & P = Rs.\,3300 \\ & A = Rs.\,3399 \\ & R = 6\% \,{\text{per}}\,{\text{annum}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{n}}\,{\text{years}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Compound}}\,{\text{interest}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{taken}}\,{\text{half - yearly}}. \\ & A = P \times {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{R}{2} \times 100} \right)} \right]^{2n}} \\ & 3399 = 3300{\left( {1 + \frac{3}{{100}}} \right)^{2n}} \\ & {\left( {1.03} \right)^{2n}} = \frac{{3399}}{{3300}} \\ & {\left( {1.03} \right)^{2n}} = {\left( {1.03} \right)^1} \\ & Thus,\,2n = 1\,year \\ & n = \frac{1}{2}{\text{year}} = 6\,{\text{months}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Rahul purchased a Maruti van for Rs. 1, 96,000 and the rate of depreciation is $$14\frac{2}{7}\%$$ per annum. Find the value of the van after two years.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Value}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{maruti}}\,{\text{Van}},\, \\ & {V_0} = Rs.\,196000 \\ & {\text{Rate}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{depreciation}},\, \\ & r = 14 {\frac{2}{7}} \% = \frac{{100}}{7}\% ; \\ & {\text{Time}},\,t = 2\,{\text{years}} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{V_1}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{value}}\,{\text{after}}\,{\text{depreciation}}. \\ & {V_1} = {V_0} \times {\left[ {1 - \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^t} \\ & {V_1} = 196000 \times {\left[ {1 - \left( {\frac{{\left( {\frac{{100}}{7}} \right)}}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^2} \\ & {V_1} = 196000 \times {\left( {1 - {\frac{1}{7}}} \right)^2} \\ & {V_1} = 196000 \times {\left( {\frac{7-1}{7}} \right)^2} \\ & {V_1} = 196000 \times {\left( {\frac{6}{7}} \right)^2} \\ & {V_1} = \frac{{\left( {196000 \times 36} \right)}}{{49}} \\ & {V_1} = Rs.\,144000 \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the rate of simple interest for the first 4 years if the sum of Rs. 360 becomes Rs. 540 in 9 years and the rate of interest for the last 5 years is 6%?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Interest}}\,{\text{for}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{last}}\,{\text{5}}\,{\text{years}} \\ & = \frac{{PTR}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{360 \times 5 \times 6}}{{100}} = Rs.\,108 \\ & {\text{Interest}}\,{\text{for}}\,{\text{year}} = 540 - 360 = 180 \\ & {\text{So,}}\,{\text{interest}}\,{\text{for}}\,{\text{first}}\,{\text{four}}\,{\text{years}} \\ & = 180 - 108 = Rs.\,72; \\ & {\text{Now,}}\,{\text{rate}}\,{\text{for}}\,{\text{first}}\,{\text{four}}\,{\text{years}} \\ & = \frac{{ {72 \times 100} }}{{360 \times 4}} \\ & = 5\% \end{aligned}$$

q: What will be the simple interest on Rs. 700 at 9% per annum for the period from February 5, 1994 to April 18, 1994?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Here,}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{interval}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{given}}\,{\text{as}}\, \\ & {\text{February}}\,5,\,1994\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{April}}\,18,\,1994 \\ & = 73\,{\text{days}} = \frac{{73}}{{365}} = 0.2\,{\text{years}}. \\ & {\text{Now}}\,{\text{interest}} = \frac{{PTR}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{ {700 \times 9 \times 0.2} }}{{100}} \\ & = Rs.\,12.60 \end{aligned}$$

q: Asif borrows Rs. 1500 from two moneylenders. He pays interest at the rate of 12% per annum for one loan and at the rate of 14% per annum for the other. The total interest he pays for the entire year is Rs. 186. How much does he borrow at the rate of 12%
s: Let Asif lent Rs. X at 14% per year. Hence, Money lent at 12% = (1500 - x); Given, total interest = Rs. 186 $${\frac{{\left( {x \times 14 \times 1} \right)}}{{100}}} \, +$$ $${\frac{{\left[ {\left( {1500 - x} \right) \times 12 \times 1} \right]}}{{100}}}$$ = 186 $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{14x}}{{100}} + \frac{{ {18000 - 12x} }}{{100}} = 186 \\ & 14x + 18000 - 12x = 186 \times 100 \\ & 2x = 18600 - 18000 \\ & x = \frac{{600}}{2} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}300 \\ & {\text{Hence, money lent}}{\kern 1pt} {\text{at }}12\% \\ & = 1500 - 300 \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,1200 \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum was invested at simple interest at a certain interest for 2 years. It would have fetched Rs. 60 more had it been invested at 2% higher rate. What was the sum?
s: Let the rate be R at which Principal P is invested for 2 years. According to question, {Interest at Rate (R + 2)}% - (interest at rate R%) = Rs. 60 $$\frac{{\left( {P \times 2 \times \left( {R + 2} \right)} \right)}}{{100}} -$$ $$\frac{{\left( {P \times 2 \times R} \right)}}{{100}}$$ $$= 60$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{ {2PR + 4P - 2PR} }}{{100}} = 60 \\ & 4P = 60 \times 100 \\ & {\text{Or}},P = \frac{{60 \times 100}}{4} \\ & {\text{Hence}},P = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,1500 \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between simple and compound interest on a sum of money at 20% per annum for 3 years is Rs. 48. What is the sum?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{sum}}\,{\text{is}}\,P. \\ & {\text{The}}\,{\text{difference}}\,{\text{between}}\,{\text{compound}}\,{\text{interest}}\,{\text{and}} \\ & \,{\text{simple}}\,{\text{interest}}\,{\text{over}}\,{\text{three}}\,{\text{years}}\,{\text{is}}\,{\text{given}}\,{\text{by}} \\ & = P\left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)2 \times \left\{ {\left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right) + 3} \right\} \\ & 48 = P \times \left( {\frac{{20}}{{100}}} \right)2 \times \left\{ {\left( {\frac{{20}}{{100}}} \right) + 3} \right\} \\ & 48 = P \times \frac{4}{{100}} \times \frac{{16}}{5} \\ & 48 = P \times \frac{{64}}{{500}} \\ & {\text{Or}},\,64P = 48 \times 500 \\ & {\text{Hence}},\,P = Rs.\,375 \end{aligned}$$

q: In what time will the simple interest on Rs. 1750 at 9% per annum be the same as that on Rs. 2500 at 10.5% per annum in 4 years?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{time}}\,{\text{is}}\,T\,{\text{years}}. \\ & {\text{According}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{questions}}, \\ & \frac{{1750 \times 9 \times T}}{{100}} = \frac{{\left( {2500 \times 10.5 \times 4} \right)}}{{100}} \\ & Or,\,T = \frac{{ {2500 \times 10.5 \times 4} }}{{1750 \times 9}} \\ & Or,\,T = 6.66 = 6\,{\text{years}}\,{\text{and}}\,8\,{\text{months}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Raju lent Rs. 400 to Ajay for 2 years and Rs. 100 to Manoj for 4 years and received together from both Rs. 60 as interest. Find the rate of interest, simple interest being calculated.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{rate}}\,{\text{is}}\,R\% \\ & {\text{According}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{question}}, \\ & \left[ {\frac{{400 \times 2 \times R}}{{100}}} \right] + \left[ {\frac{{100 \times 4 \times R}}{{100}}} \right] = 60 \\ & 8R + 4R = 60 \\ & {\text{Hence}},\,R = 5\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum becomes 4 times at simple interest in 10 years. What is the rate of interest?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {1^{{\text{st}}}}\,{\text{Method}}: \\ & {\text{Let rate is }}R\% \\ & {\text{Now}}, \\ & P = 100, \\ & A = 400, \\ & I = 400 - 100 = 300, \\ & {\text{Time}},\,T = 10\,{\text{years}} \\ & I = \frac{{PTR}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{Or}},R = \frac{{ {100 \times I} }}{{PT}} \\ & {\text{Or}},R = \frac{{ {100 \times 300} }}{{ {100 \times 10} }} \\ & {\text{Hence}},{\kern 1pt} R = 30\% \end{aligned}$$ 2 nd Method : Here, the sum become 4 times that means 100, become 400. Rate of such question is given by $$R = \frac{{{\text{interest}}}}{{{\text{time}}}} = \frac{{300}}{{10}} = 30\%$$ 3 rd Method : Here, 300% of rise in the sum so $$\begin{aligned} & 100 - - - 300\% \uparrow - - - {\kern 1pt} 400; \\ & R = {\frac{{{\text{total}}\,{\text{percentage rise}}}}{{{\text{given time}}}}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{300\% }}{{10}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 30\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of money placed at compound interest doubles itself in 4 years. In how many years will it amount to 8 times?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}, \\ & {\text{Principal}} = Rs.\,100 \\ & {\text{Amount}} = Rs.\,200 \\ & {\text{Rate}} = r\% \\ & {\text{Time}} = 4\,{\text{years}} \\ & {\text{Now}}, \\ & A = P \times {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^n} \\ & 200 = 100 \times {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^4} \\ & 2 = {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^4} - - - - - - \left( i \right) \\ & {\text{If}}\,{\text{sum}}\,{\text{become}}\,{\text{8}}\,{\text{times}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{time}}\,n\,{\text{years}} \\ & {\text{then,}} \\ & 8 = {\left( {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right)^n} \\ & {2^3} = {\left( {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right)^n} - - - - - - \left( {ii} \right) \\ & {\text{Using}}\,{\text{eqn}}\,\left( i \right)in\left( {ii} \right),\,{\text{we}}\,{\text{get}} \\ & {\left( {{{\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]}^4}} \right)^3} = {\left( {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right)^n} \\ & {\left[ {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right]^{12}} = {\left( {1 + \left( {\frac{r}{{100}}} \right)} \right)^n} \\ & {\text{Thus}},\,n = 12\,{\text{years}}. \end{aligned}$$

q: Divide Rs. 6000 into two parts so that simple interest on the first part for 2 years at 6% p.a. may be equal to the simple interest on the second part for 3 years at 8% p.a.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{1^{st}}\,{\text{part}}\,{\text{is}}\,x\,{\text{and}}\,{2^{nd}}\,{\text{part}}\,{\text{is}}\,\left( {6000 - x} \right) \\ & {\text{According}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{question}}, \\ & {\frac{{x \times 2 \times 6}}{{100}}} = \frac{{ {\left( {6000 - x} \right) \times 3 \times 8} }}{{100}} \\ & 12x = 144000 - 24x \\ & Or,\,36x = 144000 \\ & Or,\,x = \frac{{144000}}{{36}} = Rs.\,4000 \\ & {1^{st}}\,{\text{part}} = Rs.\,4000 \\ & {2^{nd}}\,{\text{part}} = Rs.\,2000 \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of money becomes $$\frac{7}{4}$$ of itself in 6 years at a certain rate of simple interest. Find the rate of interest.

q: A milkman sells cow milk at the rate of Rs. 55 litre including a profit 12 per cent. He also sells buffalo milk at the rate of Rs. 36 per litre including a profit of 20%. How much profit will he earn in five days if he sells 8 litres of cow milk and 10 litres of buffalo milk per day?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Total}}\,{\text{cow}}\,{\text{milksold}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{five}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & = 5 \times 8 = 40\,{\text{litres}} \\ & {\text{Total}}\,{\text{buffalo}}\,{\text{milk}}\,{\text{sold}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{five}}\,{\text{days}} \\ & = 5 \times 10 = 50\,{\text{litres}} \\ & {\text{Hence}}, \\ & {\text{SP}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{40}}\,{\text{litres}}\,{\text{cow}}\,{\text{milk}} \\ & = 40 \times 55 = Rs.\,2200 \\ & {\text{Hence}}, \\ & {\text{Profit}}\,{\text{on}}\,{\text{cow}}\,{\text{milk}} \\ & = \frac{{ {2200 \times 12} }}{{112}} = Rs.\,235.71 \\ & {\text{Profit}}\,{\text{on}}\,{\text{buffalo}}\,{\text{milk}} \\ & = \frac{{ {50 \times 36 \times 20} }}{{120}} = Rs.\,300 \\ & {\text{Thus}}, \\ & {\text{Total}}\,{\text{Profit}} \\ & = 235.71 + 300 = Rs.\,535.71 \end{aligned}$$

q: The population of vultures in a particular locality is decreases by certain rate of interest (compounded annually). If the current population of vultures be 29160 and the ratio of decrease in population for second year and 3rd year be 10 : 9. What was the population of vultures 3 years ago?

q: A sum fetched a total simple interest of Rs. 4016.25 at the rate of 9 p.c.p.a. in 5 years. What is the sum?

q: How much time will it take for an amount of Rs. 450 to yield Rs. 81 as interest at 4.5% per annum of simple interest?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Time}} = \left( {\frac{{100 \times 81}}{{450 \times 4.5}}} \right){\text{years}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 4\,{\text{years}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Reena took a loan of Rs. 1200 with simple interest for as many years as the rate of interest. If she paid Rs. 432 as interest at the end of the loan period, what was the rate of interest?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{rate}}\, = R\% \,{\text{and}} \\ & {\text{Time}}\,{\text{ = }}\,{\text{R}}\,{\text{years}}{\text{}} \\ & {\text{Then,}}\, {\frac{{1200 \times R \times R}}{{100}}} = 432 \\ & \Rightarrow 12{R^2} = 432 \\ & \Rightarrow {R^2} = 36 \\ & \Rightarrow R = 6 \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of Rs. 12,500 amounts to Rs. 15,500 in 4 years at the rate of simple interest. What is the rate of interest?

An automobile financier claims to be lending money at simple interest, but he includes the interest every six months for calculating the principal. If he is charging an interest of 10%, the effective rate of interest becomes:

(100 + 5 + 5.25) = Rs. 110.25 ∴ Effective rate = (110.25 - 100) = 10.25%

q: A lent Rs. 5000 to B for 2 years and Rs. 3000 to C for 4 years on simple interest at the same rate of interest and received Rs. 2200 in all from both of them as interest. The rate of interest per annum is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{rate}}\,{\text{be}}\,R\% \,{\text{p}}{\text{.a}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{Then,}} \\ & {\frac{{5000 \times R \times 2}}{{100}}} + {\frac{{3000 \times R \times 4}}{{100}}} \\ & = 2200. \\ & \Rightarrow 100R + 120R = 2200 \\ & \Rightarrow R = {\frac{{2200}}{{220}}} = 10 \\ & \therefore {\text{Rate}} = 10\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of Rs. 725 is lent in the beginning of a year at a certain rate of interest. After 8 months, a sum of Rs. 362.50 more is lent but at the rate twice the former. At the end of the year, Rs. 33.50 is earned as interest from both the loans. What was the original rate of interest?
s: Let the original rate be R%. Then, new rate = (2R)%. Note: Here, original rate is for 1 year(s); the new rate is for only 4 months i.e. $$\frac{1}{3}$$ year(s). $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\frac{{725 \times R \times 1}}{{100}}} + {\frac{{362.50 \times 2R \times 1}}{{100 \times 3}}} \\ & = 33.50 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {2175 + 725} \right)R = 33.50 \times 100 \times 3 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {2175 + 725} \right)R = 10050 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {2900} \right)R = 10050 \\ & \Rightarrow R = \frac{{10050}}{{2900}} = 3.46 \\ & \therefore \text{Original rate} = 3.46\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A person borrows Rs. 5000 for 2 years at 4% p.a. simple interest. He immediately lends it to another person at 6$$\frac{1}{4}$$ p.a for 2 years. Find his gain in the transaction per year.
s: $${\text{Gain in 2 years}}$$ $$= {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,\left[ {\left( {5000 \times \frac{{25}}{4} \times \frac{2}{{100}}} \right) - \left( {\frac{{5000 \times 4 \times 2}}{{100}}} \right)} \right]$$ $$\begin{aligned} & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,\left( {625 - 400} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}.225 \\ & \therefore {\text{Gain in 1 year}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,\left( {\frac{{225}}{2}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,112.50 \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of money becomes $$\frac{7}{6}$$ of itself in 3 years at a certain rate of simple interest. The rate of interest per annum is ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let principal = 6P}} \\ & {\text{Hence Amount}} \\ & {\text{ = 6P}} \times \frac{7}{6} = 7{\text{P}} \\ & \therefore {\text{SI = 7P}} - {\text{6P = P}} \\ & {\text{Time = 3 years}} \\ & \boxed{{\text{SI = }}\frac{{{\text{P}} \times {\text{T}} \times {\text{R}}}}{{100}}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{P = }}\frac{{6{\text{P}} \times {\text{R}} \times {\text{3}}}}{{100}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R = }}\frac{{100}}{{18}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{50}}{9} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 5\frac{5}{9}\% \end{aligned}$$ Alternate: Note: In such type of questions to save your valuable time try to think like that. \[\begin{gathered} \begin{array}{cccccccccccc} {{\text{Amount}}}&{{\text{Principal}}} \end{array} \\ {\text{ }}\underbrace {7\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{6}}}_{ + 1} \\ \end{gathered}\] $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Required rate \% }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{1}{6} \times \frac{{100}}{3} \\ & = 5\frac{5}{9}\% \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between the simple interest received from two different sources on Rs. 1500 for 3 years is Rs. 13.50. The difference between their rates of interest is ?
s: Let the rate of interest for two different sources is r 1 and r 2 respectively. $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{1500 \times {{\text{r}}_1} \times 3}}{{100}} - \frac{{1500 \times {{\text{r}}_2} \times 3}}{{100}} \\ & = 13.50 \\ & 4500{{\text{r}}_1} - 4500{{\text{r}}_2} = 1350 \\ & \left( {{{\text{r}}_1} - {{\text{r}}_2}} \right) = \frac{{1350}}{{4500}} = 0.3\% \end{aligned}$$ Hence required difference in rates = 0.3%

q: A sum of Rs. 1600 gives a simple interest of Rs. 252 in 2 years and 3 months. The rate of interest per annum is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Time = 2 years 3 months}} \\ & {\text{ = 2 + }}\frac{3}{{12}}{\text{ = }}\frac{9}{2}{\text{ years}} \\ & {\text{We know }}\boxed{{\text{SI = }}\frac{{{\text{P}} \times {\text{T}} \times {\text{R}}}}{{100}}} \\ & {\text{P = Rs 1600,}} \\ & {\text{T = }}\frac{9}{4}{\text{years,}} \\ & {\text{SI = Rs 252}} \\ & {\text{Put values in the formula ,}} \\ & \Rightarrow 252 = \frac{{1600 \times {\text{R}} \times 9}}{{100}} \\ & \Rightarrow 252 = 36{\text{R}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R = }}\frac{{252}}{{36}} = 7\% \end{aligned}$$

q: Ram borrows Rs. 520 from Gaurav at a simple interest of 13% per annum. What amount of money should Ram pay to Gaurav after 6 months to be absolved of the debt?.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{P}} = {\text{Rs}}.\,520, \\ & {\text{R}} = 13\% \\ & {\text{T}} = \frac{1}{2}yr. \\ & \therefore {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.}} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{520 \times 13}}{{100 \times 2}}} \right) \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}33.80 \\ & {\text{Hence, amount after 6 months}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {520 + 33.80} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}553.80 \end{aligned}$$

q: What will be the simple interest earned on an amount of Rs. 16,800 in 9 months at the rate of $$6\frac{1}{4}$$ % p.a. ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{P}} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}16800 \\ & {\text{R}} = 6\frac{1}{4}\% = \frac{{25}}{4}\% \\ & {\text{T}} = 9\,{\text{mths}} = \frac{3}{4}{\text{yr}}{\text{.}} \\ & \therefore {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.}} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {16800 \times \frac{{25}}{4} \times \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{{100}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,787.50 \end{aligned}$$

q: The simple interest on a sum of money is $$\frac{4}{9}$$ of the principal and the number of years is equal to the rate percent per annum. The rate per annum is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the principal}} \\ & {\text{ = 9 units }} \\ & {\text{Hence simple interest}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{4}{9} \times {\text{9 = 4 units}} \\ & {\text{Let,}} \\ & {\text{Rate of interest = R\% }} \\ & {\text{R = T (given)}} \\ & {\text{By using formula}} \\ & \boxed{{\text{SI = }}\frac{{{\text{P}} \times {\text{T}} \times {\text{R}}}}{{100}}} \\ & 4 = \frac{{9 \times {\text{R}} \times {\text{R}}}}{{100}} \\ & {{\text{R}}^2} = \frac{{400}}{9} \\ & {\text{R = }}\frac{{20}}{3} = 6\frac{2}{3}\% \end{aligned}$$

q: At what rate percent per annum will the simple interest on a sum of money be $$\frac{2}{5}$$ of the principal amount in 10 years ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let principal = 5 units}} \\ & {\text{Hence interest}} \\ & {\text{ = 5}} \times \frac{2}{5} \\ & {\text{ = 2 units}} \\ & {\text{Time = 10 years}} \\ & {\text{By using formula, }} \\ & {\text{Rate\% = }}\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{{100}}{{10}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{ = 4\% }} \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of Rs. 1750 is divided into two parts such that the interests on the first part at 8% simple interest per annum and that on the other part at 6% simple interest per annum are equal. The interest on each part ( in Rupees) is ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Principal = Rs}}{\text{. 1750}} \\ & {\text{Let the first part = }}x \\ & {\text{Hence second part}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {1750 - x} \right) \\ & {\text{According to the question,}} \\ & \Rightarrow x \times \frac{8}{{100}} \times 1 = \left( {1750 - x} \right) \times \frac{6}{{100}} \times 1 \\ & \Rightarrow 4x = 5250 - 3x \\ & \Rightarrow 7x = 5250 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 750 \\ & {\text{First part = Rs}}{\text{. 750}} \\ & \therefore {\text{ Second part}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {1750 - 750} \right) \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 1000}} \\ & {\text{Required interest}} \\ & {\text{ = 750}} \times \frac{8}{{100}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 60}} \end{aligned}$$ Alternate Note : In such type of questions to save your valuable time follow the given below method. Let, Principal = 100 units in both cases 1 st part 2 nd part Total Principal → 100 ×3 : 100 ×4 +→ 700 units Interest → 8 ×3 : 6 ×4 Note : Interest is same in both cases According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{700 units = Rs}}{\text{. 1750}} \\ & {\text{1 unit = Rs}}{\text{. }}\frac{{1750}}{{700}} \\ & {\text{24 units = Rs}}{\text{. }}\frac{{1750}}{{700}} \times 24 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 60}} \\ & {\text{Hence, required interest}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 60}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A person borrows Rs. 5000 for 2 year at 4% p.a. simple interest. He immediately lends it to another person at $$6\frac{1}{4}$$ % p.a. for 2 years. Find his gain in the transaction per year.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Gain in 2 years}} \\ & = {\left( {5000 \times \frac{{25}}{4} \times \frac{2}{{100}}} \right) - \left( {\frac{{5000 \times 4 \times 2}}{{100}}} \right)} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {625 - 400} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}225 \\ & \therefore {\text{Gain 1 year}} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{225}}{2}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}112.50 \end{aligned}$$

q: Ramakant invested amounts in two different schemes A and B for five years in the ratio of 5 : 4 respectively. Scheme A offers 8% simple interest and bonus equal to 20% of the amount of interest earned in 5 years on maturity. Scheme B offers 9% simple interest. If the amount invested in scheme A was Rs. 20000, what was the total amount received on maturity from both the schemes?
s: Let the amounts invested in schemes A and B be Rs. 5x and 4x respectively. then, 5x = 20000 ⇒ x = 4000 ∴ Amount invested in scheme B = Rs. 16000 Total interest received on maturity $$= {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left[ {{\text{120}}\% {\text{ of}}\left( {\frac{{{\text{20000}} \times {\text{8}} \times {\text{5}}}}{{{\text{100}}}}} \right) + \left( {\frac{{{\text{16000}} \times {\text{9}} \times {\text{5}}}}{{{\text{100}}}}} \right)} \right]$$ $$\begin{aligned} & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,\left( {{\text{120}}\% \,{\text{of}}\,{\text{8000}} + {\text{7200}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,\left( {{\text{9600}} + {\text{7200}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{16800}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Total amount}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,\left( {{\text{20000}} + {\text{16000}} + {\text{16800}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{52800}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of Rs. 1550 was lent partly at 5% and partly at 8% simple interest. The total interest received after 3 years is Rs. 300. The ratio of money lent at 5% to that at 8% is = ?
s: Let the sum at 8% be Rs. x Let the sum at 5% be 1550 - x According to the given condition, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{{\text{x}} \times 8 \times 3}}{{100}} + \frac{{\left( {1550 - {\text{x}}} \right) \times 5 \times 3}}{{100}} = 300 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{24{\text{x}} + \left( {1550 - {\text{x}}} \right) \times 15}}{{100}} = 300 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{24{\text{x}} + 23250 - 15{\text{x}}}}{{100}} = 300 \\ & \Rightarrow 24{\text{x}} - 15{\text{x}} = 30000 - 23250 \\ & \Rightarrow 24{\text{x}} - 15{\text{x}} = 6750 \\ & \Rightarrow 9{\text{x}} = 6750 \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{x}} = \frac{{6750}}{9} = 750 \\ & \frac{{{\text{Money lent at 5}}\% }}{{{\text{Money lent at 8}}\% }} \\ & = \frac{{1550 - 750}}{{750}} \\ & = \frac{{800}}{{750}} \\ & = \frac{{16}}{{15}} \\ & = 16:15 \end{aligned}$$

q: A money lender finds that due to fall in the annual rate of interest from 8% to $${\text{7}}\frac{3}{4}{\text{\%,}}$$ his yearly income diminishes by Rs. 61.50. His capital is = ?

q: If the simple interest on a sum of money for 15 months at $${\text{7}}\frac{1}{2}$$ % per annum exceeds the simple interest on the same sum for 8 months at $${\text{12}}\frac{1}{2}$$ % per annum by Rs. 32.50, then the sum of money ( In Rs.) is ?

q: If simple interest on Rs. 600 for 4 years and on Rs. 600 for 2 years combined together is Rs.180, find the rate of interest.

q: A certain sum of money becomes three times of itself in 20 years at simple interest. In how many years does it become double itself at the same rate of simple interest ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let principal = P}} \\ & \therefore {\text{amount = 3P}} \\ & {\text{Interest = 3P}} - {\text{P}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{ = 2P}} \\ & {\text{According to the question,}} \\ & {\text{2P = }}\frac{{{\text{P}} \times {\text{R}} \times {\text{20}}}}{{100}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{R = 10\% }} \end{aligned}$$ Let after t years it will become double $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Hence,}} \\ & {\text{Interest = 2P}} - {\text{P = P}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{P = }}\frac{{{\text{P}} \times 10 \times {\text{t}}}}{{100}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{t = 10 years}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A person borrows some money for 5 years and ratio of loan amount : total interest amount is 5 : 2. Then find the ratio of loan amount : interest rate is equal to = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Loan Amount}}:{\text{Total Interest}} \\ & {\text{5}}:{\text{2}} \\ & {\text{Principal}} \to {\text{5}} \\ & {\text{Interest for 1 year}} \Rightarrow {\text{2}} \\ & {\text{Interest for 5 year}} \Rightarrow {\text{10}} \\ & {\text{10}} = \frac{{5 \times {\text{R}} \times 5}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{R}}\% = 40\% \\ & = \frac{{40}}{{100}} = \frac{2}{5} \\ & {\text{P}}:{\text{R}} = 5:\frac{2}{5} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 25:2 \end{aligned}$$

q: The effective annual rate of interest, corresponding to a nominal rate of 6% per annum payable half yearly is = ?

q: Veena obtained an amount of Rs. 8376 as simple interest on a certain amount at 8 p.c.p.a. after 6 years. what is the amount invested by veena?

q: At which sum the simple interest at the rate of $$3\frac{3}{4}$$ % per annum will be Rs. 210 in $$2\frac{1}{3}$$ years?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.}} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 210}} \\ & {\text{R}} = 3\frac{3}{4}\% = \frac{{15}}{4}\% \\ & {\text{T}} = {\text{2}}\frac{{\text{1}}}{{\text{3}}}{\text{years}} = \frac{7}{3}{\text{years}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Sum}} = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{100 \times 210}}{{\frac{{15}}{4} \times \frac{7}{3}}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{100 \times 210 \times 4 \times 3}}{{15 \times 7}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}2400 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the simple interest for 6 years be equal to 30% of the principal, it will be equal to the principal after = ?

q: Rs. 1000 is invested at 5% per annum simple interest. If the interest is added to the principal after every 10 years, the amount will become Rs. 2000 after = ?

(2000}} - {\text{1500)}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 500}} \\ & {\text{Required time }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{500}}{{1500}} \times \frac{{100}}{5} \\ & = \frac{{100}}{15} \\ & = \frac{{20}}{3} \\ & = 6\frac{2}{3}{\text{ years}} \\ & {\text{Total time}} \\ & = \left( {10 + 6\frac{2}{3}} \right){\text{years}} \\ & {\text{ = 16}}\frac{2}{3}{\text{ years}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Rs. 6200 amounts to Rs. 9176 in 4 years at simple interest. If the interest rate is increased by 3% it would amount to how much?

q: The simple interest accrued on a certain principal in 5 years at the rate of 12 p.c.p.a. is Rs.1536. what amount of simple interest would one get if one invests Rs.1000 more than the previous principal for 2 years and at the same rate p.c.p.a. ?

q: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 5% p.a. for 8 years is Rs. 840. At what rate of interest the same account of interest can be received on the same sum after 5 years?

q: Rs. 6000 becomes Rs. 7200 in 4 years. If the rate becomes 1.5 times of itself, the amount of the same principal in 5 years will be = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Principal}}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Amount}} \\ & \underbrace {\,\,\,\,\,{\text{6000}}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{7200}}\,\,\,\,\,}_{ + 1200} \\ & {\text{By using formula,}} \\ & {\text{Rate }}\% \\ & = \frac{{1200}}{{6000}} \times \frac{{100}}{4} \\ & {\text{ = 5}}\% \\ & {\text{New rate}}\% \\ & = {\text{5}} \times \frac{3}{2} = {\text{7}}{\text{.5}}\% \\ & {\text{Interest after 5 years}} \\ & = \frac{{6000 \times 7.5 \times 5}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 2250}} \\ & {\text{Hence,}} \\ & {\text{amount }} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {6000 + 2250} \right) \\ & {\text{ = Rs 8250}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Simple interest on Rs. 500 for 4 years at 6.25% per annum is equal to the simple interest on Rs. 400 at 5% per annum for a certain period of time. The period of time is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the required time = t years }} \\ & {\text{According to the question,}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{500 \times 4 \times 6.25}}{{100}} = \frac{{400 \times 5 \times {\text{t}}}}{{100}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5 \times 4 \times 625 = 400 \times 5 \times {\text{t}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\text{t = }}\frac{{625}}{{100}} = \frac{{25}}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\text{t}} = 6\frac{1}{4}{\text{years}} \end{aligned}$$

q: With a given rate of simple interest, the ratio of principal and amount for a certain period of time is 4 : 5. After 3 years with the same rate of interest, the ratio of the principal and amount becomes 5 : 7. The rate of interest is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{{\text{Principal}}}}{{{\text{Amount}}}} = \frac{{4 \times 5}}{{5 \times 5}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{20}}{{25}} \\ & {\text{After three year}} \\ & \frac{{\text{P}}}{{\text{A}}} = \frac{{5 \times 4}}{{7 \times 4}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{20}}{{28}} \\ & {\text{In three year S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.}} \\ & = 28x - 25x \\ & = 3x \\ & \text{So, the required interest will be} \\ & 3x = \frac{{20x \times {\text{R}} \times 3}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{R}} = 5\% \end{aligned}$$

q: If x, y, z are three sums of money such that y is the simple interest on x, z is the simple interest on y for the same time and at the same rate of interest, then we have.
s: Let time be T years and rate be R% p.a. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Then, }}y{\text{ is the S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. on x}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{x{\text{RT}}}}{{100}} = y......(i) \\ & {\text{And, }}z{\text{ is the S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. on y}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{y{\text{RT}}}}{{100}} = z \\ & \Rightarrow y = \frac{{100z}}{{RT}}......(ii) \\ & {\text{From (i) and (ii) we have:}} \\ & \frac{{x{\text{RT}}}}{{100}} = \frac{{100z}}{{{\text{RT}}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{x{{\text{R}}^2}{{\text{T}}^2}}}{{{{\left( {100} \right)}^2}}} = z \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{y^2}}}{x} = z \\ & \Rightarrow {y^2}= xz \end{aligned}$$

q: What equal installment of annual payment will discharge a debt which is due as Rs. 848 at the end of 4 years at 4% per annum simple interest ?
s: Note : In such type of questions to save your valuable time follow the given below method. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Value of installment}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{{\text{Principal}} \times {\text{100}}}}{{{\text{Time}} \times {\text{100}} + \left( {{{\text{t}}_{{\text{n - 1}}}} + {{\text{t}}_{{\text{n - 2}}}}...1} \right) \times {\text{Rate}}\% }} \\ & {\text{Principal = Rs}}{\text{. 848}} \\ & {\text{Rate = 4}}\% \\ & {\text{Time = 4 year}} \\ & {\text{Installment}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{848 \times 100}}{{4 \times 100 + \left( {3 + 2 + 1} \right) \times 4}}{\text{ }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{848 \times 100}}{{\left( {400 + 24} \right)}}{\text{ }} \\ & = \frac{{848 \times 100}}{{424}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 200}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A sum of money at a certain rate per annum of simple interest doubles in the 5 years and at a different rate becomes three times in 12 years. The lower rate of interest per annum is = ?
s: Rate of interest $$= \frac{{100(x - 1)}}{t}\%$$ Where x is the no. of times the sum becomes of itself. Here the sum is getting 3 times. Therefore, x = 3 Where t is the time taken by sum to become x times of itself. Here, t = 12 years By the short trick approach, we get $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{100(3 - 1)}}{{12}} \\ & = \frac{{200}}{{12}} \\ & = \frac{{50}}{3} = 16\frac{2}{3}\% \end{aligned}$$ Alternative Method : Let the principal be P and in the 2nd scenario, SI = 2P $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Rate}} = \frac{{{\text{SI}} \times 100}}{{{\text{Principal}} \times {\text{Time}}}} \\ & = \frac{{2{\text{P}} \times 100}}{{{\text{P}} \times 12}} \\ & = \frac{{50}}{3} \\ & = 16\frac{2}{3}\% \end{aligned}$$

q: If Rs. 12000 is divided into two parts such that the simple interest on the first part for 3 years at 12% per annum is equal to the simple interest on the second part for $$4\frac{1}{2}$$ years at 16% per annum, the greater part is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the first part = Rs}}{\text{. }}x \\ & \therefore {\text{Hence second part}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {12000 - x} \right) \\ & {\text{According to the question,}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{x \times 12 \times 3}}{{100}} = \frac{{\left( {12000 - x} \right) \times 9 \times 16}}{{2 \times 100}} \\ & \Rightarrow 36x = 72\left( {12000 - x} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow x = 24000 - 2x \\ & \Rightarrow 3x = 24000 \\ & \Rightarrow x = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 8000}} \\ & {{\text{1}}^{{\text{st}}}}{\text{ part = Rs}}{\text{. 8000}} \\ & {{\text{2}}^{{\text{nd}}}}{\text{ part}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. }}\left( {12000 - 8000} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 4000 }} \\ & {\text{Hence maximum part}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 8000}} \end{aligned}$$ Alternate Note : In such type of questions to save your valuable time follow the given below method. Let two parts P 1 and P 2 respectively According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {{\text{P}}_1} \times \frac{{36}}{{100}} \times 1 = {{\text{P}}_2} \times \frac{9}{2} \times \frac{{16}}{{100}} \times 1 \\ & \Rightarrow {{\text{P}}_1} \times 4 = 8{{\text{P}}_2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{{\text{P}}_1}}}{{{{\text{P}}_2}}} = \frac{2}{1} \\ & \Rightarrow {{\text{P}}_1}{\text{:}}{{\text{P}}_2} = 2:1 \\ & {\text{Hence greater part}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{12000}}{{\left( {2 + 1} \right)}} \times 2 \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}8000 \end{aligned}$$

q: An automobile financier claims to be lending money at simple interest, but he includes the interest every six months for calculating the principal. If he is charging an interest of 10%, the effective rate of interest becomes
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let the sum be Rs}}{\text{.100}}{\text{}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.for first 6 months}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{100 \times 10 \times 1}}{{100 \times 2}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}5 \\ & {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.for last 6 months}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{105 \times 10 \times 1}}{{100 \times 2}}} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}5.25 \\ & So, \\ & {\text{Amount at the end of 1year}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {100 + 5 + 5.25} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\,110.25 \\ & \therefore {\text{Effective rate}} \\ & = \left( {110.25 - {\text{100}}} \right) \\ & = 10.25\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A lent Rs. 5000 to B for 2 years and Rs. 3000 to C for 4 years on simple interest at the same rate of interest and received Rs. 2200 in all from both as interest. The rate of interest per annum is = ?

q: What annual installment will discharge a debt of Rs. 6450 due in 4 years at 5% simple interest = ?

q: A sum of money lent out at simple interest amounts to Rs. 720 after 2 years and to Rs.1020 after a further period of 5 years. The sum is

q: A sum of money becomes Rs. 20925 in 2 years and Rs. 24412.50 in 5 years. Find the rate of interest and the sum of money.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. }}{\text{for 3 years}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {24412.50 - 20925} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}3487.50 \\ & {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. }}{\text{for 2 years}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{3487.50}}{3} \times 2} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}2325 \\ & \therefore \text{Principal} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {20925 - 2325} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}18600 \\ & {\text{Hence,}} \\ & {\text{rate}} = \left( {\frac{{100 - 2325}}{{18600 \times 2}}} \right)\% \\ & = 6.25\% \end{aligned}$$

q: In how many years will a sum of money double itself at 18.75% per annum simple interest?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let sum = Rs}}{\text{. }}x{\text{}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{. = Rs}}{\text{. }}x{\text{}} \\ & \therefore \text{Time} = \left( {\frac{{100 \times {\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.}}}}{{{\text{P}} \times {\text{R}}}}} \right) \\ & = \left( {\frac{{100 \times x}}{{x \times 18.75}}} \right){\text{years}} \\ & = \frac{{26}}{3}{\text{years}} \\ & = 5\frac{1}{3}{\text{years}} \\ & = {\text{5 years 4 months}}{\text{}} \end{aligned}$$

q: In how many years will the simple interest on a sum of money be equal to the principal at the rate of $$16\frac{2}{3}$$ % per annum ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{16}}\frac{2}{3} = \frac{{1 \to {\text{ Interest}}}}{{6 \to {\text{ Principal }}}} \\ & {\text{Let principal = 6}} \\ & {\text{Interest = 6}} \\ & {\text{Time = t years}} \\ & {\text{By using formula }} \\ & {\text{6}} = \frac{{6 \times 50 \times {\text{t}}}}{{3 \times 100}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{t}} = 6\,{\text{years}} \end{aligned}$$ Alternate Note : In such type of questions to save your valuable time think like the given way. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Rate}}\% \\ & {\text{ = 16}}\frac{2}{3}\% = \frac{{1 \to {\text{ Interest}}}}{{6 \to {\text{ Principal }}}} \\ & {\text{Represent for 1 years}} \\ & {\text{According to the question,}} \\ & {\text{Principal = Interest}} \\ & {\text{6 = 1}} \times {\text{6}} \\ & {\text{Hence,}} \\ & {\text{Time = 1}} \times {\text{6}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{ = 6 years}} \end{aligned}$$ Note : If interest will be six times then time will also be six times.

q: A sum of money was invested at a certain rate of simple interest for 2 years. Had it been invested at 1% higher rate, it would have fetched Rs. 24 more interest. The sum of money is ?

q: A man invests half of his capital at the rate of 10% per annum, one - third at 9% and the rest at 12% per annum. The average rate of interest per annum, which he gets is = ?

q: A sum of money at simple interest doubles in 7 years. It will become four times in:
